newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen-Late euro better than weak euro.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen-Late euro better than weak euro.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Monday the spectre of a failed timely launch for Europe's monetary union or a weak common currency would be far worse than a delay of the launch date.
Jochimsen told a news conference that it was indispensable that monetary union be based on solid foundations.

"If after the start of monetary union it turns out that the foundations do not yet support -- if the euro either fails, drifts apart, or becomes a weak currency -- the damage to European integration would be far worse than for example a limited and conditional postponement," he said.

The launch of the single currency demanded that members were chosen in accordance with strict and stability-oriented criteria and not by resorting to creative accounting or generous interpretation on the Maastricht Treaty criteria.
"The fact that this awareness is less and less prevalent is definitely not helping monetary union gain the necessary credibility among citizens," Jochimsen said.

Asked if he agreed with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's statement that the Maastricht Treaty's deficit goal be no more than 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, Jochimsen said the goal should be interpreted "in a stability-oriented way without fiddling".
"I always regarded it as relating to the Treaty which calls for a stability-oriented interpretation and no fiddling around," he said.
Jochimsen said what counted was the assessment of whether convergence was solid and lasting and not whether a "point-landing" had been reached.
He also said he was opposed to risking the stability of the currency union for the sake of allowing a large group of members to take part from the start.
"People say one needs a large starting group. I would say if this entailed risking stability and long-term stability that would be too high a price to pay."
